title: Contextual rail collapsing and route segmentation — notes and backlog
content:
Context: quick working doc capturing observations, wireframe variants, and a pragmatic backlog for a navigation refresh focused on contextual collapsing of the left rail and segmentation of routes by task surface. Goal is to reduce noise for high-frequency users while preserving discoverability for infrequent or admin personas. This is intentionally rough — meant for sync with SRE/product/design before formal PRD.

Problem statements (observed):
- Left rail currently exposes ~18 top-level items; cognitive load is high for engineers who only use 4–5 routes regularly.
- Deep routes live under ambiguous parent labels (e.g., 'observability' mixes traces, logs, and model metrics).
- Small screens and embedded views (embedded tenant consoles for partners) lose important controls — we need a compact mode with contextual affordances.
- Onboarding users and infrequent admins struggle to find rollout controls and model pinning — low click-to-success rates.

Design goals / success metrics (experiment-driven):
- Primary metric: reduce median time-to-target-route by 25% for power users in 4–6 week A/B test.
- Secondary: reduce nav interactions per session for >50% of sessions by 1 click.
- Maintain or improve first-time-task completion for new users (onboarding flows) — measured by task success on checklist.
- Accessibility: ensure keyboard-only collapse/expand and focused aria live regions for route changes.

Concepts / patterns we want to explore: 
1) Contextual Rail Collapse (CRC): the left rail visually collapses to compact icons by default. When user selects a model, route labels rehydrate to show only routes relevant to the selected model or project.
   - State model: global collapsed / expanded + per-project contextual expansion.
   - Triggering signals: active project, last-used routes, role (admin vs dev), route frequency heuristic.
   - UX affordance: hover/keyboard reveal, persistent short tooltip, single animation for reflow.

2) Route Segmentation (task-first grouping): convert flat nav into a task-first grouping: Observability, Deploy, Model Management, Cost & Billing, Admin. Each group surface presents a short list with a horizontal overflow for secondary actions.
   - Benefit: reduces scanning time by grouping related activities.

3) Micro-hub pages: small hub pages that summarize the subroutes for a task without full page load (panel overlay with quick-actions). Useful for heavy actions like 'rollout' and 'rollback'.

Wireframe variants (quick notes):
- Variant A: Compact-with-context (default collapsed). Icons + a single adaptive band that lists 3 contextual routes. Clicking chevron expands full rail.
  - Example: select project -> band shows: Instances | Queues | Recent Jobs.
  - Good for power users, less discoverable for new users.

- Variant B: Task-tiles hybrid. Left rail shows grouped tiles (Observability, Deploy, Models). Each tile expands inline to show up to 6 routes. On small screens tile becomes an accordion.
  - Good: clear grouping; visual affordance for new users.

- Variant C: Railless primary + top breadcrumb + command palette emphasis. Moves away from persistent left rail for low-density screens; relies on quick open and sticky crumbs.
  - Good for minimal UIs and third-party embedding; riskier for discoverability.

Wireframe annotations (for design/dev pairing):
- Keyboard behavior: Tab lands on rail icon; Enter/Space toggles expansion; Arrow keys cycle contexts.
- Focus management: when micro-hub opens, focus to first action button; on close return focus to original icon.
- Animation: 120–160ms cubic-bezier easing to avoid layout jank. Avoid animating width that causes reflow of content area; prefer overlay/translate.

Routing and URL model:
- Keep canonical URLs for every surface. When rail collapses or context switches, route should not change unless user navigates. Context is client-side state derived from project ID and last-route.
- Introduce a route namespace for 'task hubs' e.g., /hubs/observability?project=proj-id to allow direct linking to micro-hubs.

Backlog (rough groom, prioritized):
1) PROJ-847: CRC experiment scaffold (epic) — create server feature flags, telemetry hooks for nav interactions, API to fetch contextual route lists. Priority: P0. Est: 5 sprint points.
2) PROJ-848: Compact icon set and tooltip microcopy — finalize icons, a11y labels, hover states, and tooltip copy. Priority: P1. Est: 2 points.
3) PROJ-849: Micro-hub component + focus behavior — implement overlay panel, quick-action buttons, and keyboard support. Priority: P1. Est: 8 points.
4) PROJ-850: Route grouping & rehome audit — product/design to propose new group names and migration plan. Priority: P0. Est: 3 points.
5) PROJ-852: A/B experiment wiring + metrics dashboard — define segments, track time-to-route, clicks, and DCO. Priority: P0. Est: 3 points.
6) PROJ-853: Embedding small-screen behavior — compact-only mode for partner embeds and iFrame sizing API. Priority: P2. Est: 4 points.

Acceptance criteria (for initial experiment rollout):
- CRC default collapsed state is available under feature flag and enabled for 10% of eligible crews.
- Telemetry events: nav_open, nav_select(route_id), nav_expand, nav_context_change are emitted and documented.
- No regressions on keyboard-only navigation and screen reader flows (a11y test checklist passes).
- Performance: first meaningful paint delta < 10% compared to baseline for typical pages.

Open questions / discussion items: 
- How do we surface cross-project routes (billing, org settings) when project context hides them? Idea: 'Global' quick-toggle at top of rail.
- Role-based default: should admins default to expanded rail? Or let them opt-in?
- Persistence: store per-user preference in account settings vs ephemeral local storage. Tradeoffs: multi-device sync vs offline complexity.

Experiment plan (high level):
Week 0: QA + internal dogfood run with platform and solutions eng.
Week 1–3: Ramp 10% cohorts; collect telemetry and session replays.
Week 4–6: Measure primary metric and collect qualitative feedback via microsurveys. If positive, expand rollout to 30% and iterate microcopy/iconography.

Notes to design/dev pair: attach prototype link and annotate expected CSS variables for compact mode (nav-width-collapsed: 56px; nav-width-expanded: 240px). Avoid changing global layout grid. Use CSS transform for micro-hub overlay.

Quick reminders and follow-ups:
- Jon to add telemetry schema in PROJ-847.
- Maya to draft copy variations for tooltips and hub headers.
- Leah to coordinate accessibility review with SRE for focus traps.

References and related files:
- Existing sitemap audit: /shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/route-mapping-and-compact-hub-proposal-june-2024.json (see overlap, but this doc is focused on contextual collapse and experimental backlog).
- Figma prototypes: see linked_artifacts above.

Short-term deliverable for next sync (1 week): a short prototype showing Variant A with two contextual signals (last-used routes, admin role) and a minimal telemetry ping attached.

Unpolished brainstorm leftovers (notes to self):
- Consider 'pin' affordance on route band so users can keep common routes visible across projects.
- Could combine with command-pallet shortcuts: typed prefix to reveal matching task hub.
- If we move to railless later, preserve breadcrumbs and a visible affordance to open the command palette.

End of doc.
